This cookbook provides practical, reproducible examples for using the Cloud Optical-array probe Processing Software (COPS).
The focus is on hands-on notebooks that demonstrate how to process and analyze optical array probe data.

The goal of this cookbook is to provide a comprehensive guide for researchers and developers working with COPS.
By the end of the cookbook, readers will be able to:

Understand the structure of a reproducible scientific workflow

Run and modify Jupyter notebooks interactively

Adapt the provided examples to their own research or applications
This cookbook is organized into the following sections:
This section explains how to cite the cookbook and the COPS software.
This section verifies the COPS installation and establishes the environment expected by future workflow notebooks.

Run the notebooks locally with a COPS source checkout:

Clone the repository:git clone https://github.com/huangynj/cookbook_test.git
cd cookbook_test

Create the environment:conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate cookbook-dev

If the environment already exists, update it instead:conda env update -f environment.yml --prune
conda activate cookbook-dev

Install COPS from source:python -m pip install -e ../COPS

If the COPS checkout is somewhere else, replace ../COPS with that path.

Start the server:myst start

This will start a local web server and open the cookbook in your browser.

Note: Do not use pip install cops for this cookbook. The cops package name on PyPI currently points to unrelated cloud-infrastructure software. Install the local COPS source checkout instead.

If you use this cookbook in your research, please cite it as follows:

Huang, Y. (2026). COPS Cookbook. 

https://​github​.com​/huangynj​/cookbook​_test

Please also cite the COPS software itself:

Huang, Y. (2026). Cloud Optical-array probe Processing Software (COPS), Version 0.0.1. Source distribution.
Welcome to the COPS Cookbook! This collection of notebooks is designed to help you get started with the Cloud Optical-array probe Processing Software (COPS).
COPS is a software package for processing and analyzing data from optical array probes (OAPs) used in cloud microphysics research.

The current cookbook starts with a reproducible installation check. Future workflow chapters can build from this setup to cover:

Reading OAP data files

Visualizing particle images

Calculating particle size distributions

Advanced analysis techniques

To follow along, you will need:

A basic understanding of Python

The cookbook-dev environment from environment.yml

A source installation of the COPS package, for example python -m pip install -e ../COPS

try:
    import cops
except ImportError as exc:
    raise ImportError(
        "COPS is not installed. Recreate or update the cookbook environment, "
        "install the local COPS source with `python -m pip install -e ../COPS`, "
        "then restart this kernel."
    ) from exc

expected_attrs = ("analysis", "io", "variables")
if not all(hasattr(cops, attr) for attr in expected_attrs):
    raise ImportError(
        "The imported 'cops' package is not the Cloud Optical-array probe "
        "Processing Software. Do not use `pip install cops`; use the "
        "environment.yml dependency instead."
    )

version = getattr(cops, "__version__", "unknown")
location = getattr(cops, "__file__", "unknown")
print(f"COPS version: {version}")
print(f"COPS module: {location}")
